Angles written ∠ are read from the figure. ∡(a, b) is the angle through which line a must be turned counter-clockwise to become parallel to b, taken modulo 180°; ∡XYZ means ∡(YX, YZ). These angles do not depend on how the figure is drawn. Directed angles are needed only in step 8, where the figure-angle form would depend on the configuration. Let ω₂ be the circle (CNR), with center O₂; P lies on ω₂. Let F be the foot of the perpendicular from B to AR.

Plan: it suffices to show that NC ∥ OF, R, N, F, O are concyclic and A, F, R, P are collinear.

1. BC is a diameter, so ∠BNC = 90°. (1)

2. We show that F, N, B, A are concyclic:

∠BFA = 90°    [BF ⟂ AR]
     = ∠BNA    [∠BNC = 90°, by (1)]

So F, N, B, A are concyclic. (2)

3. AR bisects ∠BAC, so ∠FAC = ∠BAF. F, N, B, A concyclic, by (2), so FN = BF (equal arcs and chords). (3)

4. By (3), OB = ON and FB = FN, so OF is the perpendicular bisector of BN; hence OF ⟂ BN. (4)

5. NC ⟂ NB, by (1) and OF ⟂ NB, by (4), so NC ∥ OF. (5)

6. We show that R, N, F, O are concyclic:

∠RFN = ∠MBN    [F, N, B, A concyclic, by (2)]
     = 180° − ½·∠MON    [central angle ∠MON = 2∠MBN]
     = 180° − ∠RON    [OR bisects ∠MON]

So R, N, F, O are concyclic. (6)

7. AB·AM = AC·AN (power of the point A with respect to (BMCN)). P, R, M, B concyclic, P, R, N, C on ω₂, A, B, M collinear and A, N, C collinear, so A, F, R, P are collinear (the radical axis theorem). (7)

8. We show that P lies on the line BC:

∡PCB = ∡NCO + ∡PRN    [P, R, N, C on ω₂]
     = ∡ONC + ∡PRN    [OC = ON]
     = ∡NOF + ∡PRN    [NC ∥ OF, by (5)]
     = ∡PRF    [R, N, F, O concyclic, by (6)]
     = 0°    [A, F, R, P collinear, by (7)]

So P lies on the line BC, as required. ∎
